narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the significant widening of the pay gap between American CEOs and workers over time.

units.meaning: The CEO-worker pay gap shows a broad upward widening over time, with later relative values much higher than early ones.
accepted_routes: The relative pay gap becomes substantially larger from the early part of the series to the later part.
There is a strong overall upward widening over the timeline.
Late values are much higher than early values, showing a growing gap.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A clear upward movement from early low values to much higher later values must be visible.
units.temporal_anchor: Opening clause about the pay gap growing over time.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video convey the overall upward widening even if it omits the post-peak decline?

units.meaning: The early portion of the series is low and relatively flat, staying around 0.11-0.15 before the marked 1990 point at 0.18.
accepted_routes: Early on, the gap is low, around 0.11 to 0.15 on the relative scale.
The series starts near 0.12 and stays relatively flat before the steep rise.
The 1990 marked point is 0.18, only slightly above the early low range.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The early portion must appear low and comparatively flat before the later rise.
units.temporal_anchor: Initial part of the narration before the growth is emphasized.
units.reviewer_question: Is showing the low early baseline obligatory, or can the video start at the steep growth phase?

units.meaning: After the marked 1990 point, the relative gap accelerates sharply from 0.18 through 0.25, 0.40, 0.60, 0.75 and up to 0.95.
accepted_routes: After the 1990 mark, the gap climbs rapidly from 0.18 to 0.95 on the relative scale.
The steepest increase happens in the later part of the series, moving from about 0.18 to 0.95.
The series accelerates after 1990 before reaching its peak.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The steepest upward section must be visible after the 1990 marker and before the maximum.
units.temporal_anchor: Clause describing the rapid growth of the gap.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the steep post-1990 acceleration, or is the overall endpoint comparison sufficient?

units.meaning: The series reaches its highest relative value at 0.95, about eight times the early 0.12 level.
accepted_routes: The largest gap in the series is 0.95 on the relative scale.
The peak is nearly eight times the starting relative level.
The maximum is about 0.95, far above the early 0.12 baseline.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A distinct maximum near 0.95 must be visible, much higher than the early baseline.
units.temporal_anchor: Clause describing the gap growing to its most extreme point.
units.reviewer_question: Should the peak be shown explicitly as a maximum, or is the final endpoint comparison enough?

units.meaning: After the peak, the relative gap declines to about 0.55-0.65 and ends around 0.65, still roughly five times the early 0.12 baseline but below the 0.95 peak.
accepted_routes: After peaking, the relative gap falls to about 0.55-0.65 and ends at 0.65.
The final value is 0.65, below the 0.95 peak but still roughly five times the initial 0.12.
The series declines after its maximum but remains elevated relative to the early baseline.
units.visual_evidence_rule: After the maximum, the visual must show a decline to about 0.55-0.65 and an ending near 0.65.
units.temporal_anchor: No direct narration clause; optional data-backed elaboration after the growth statement.
units.reviewer_question: Should the post-peak decline be treated as required because the table shows it, or optional because the intent emphasizes widening?

optional_valid: The early segment contains a small dip to 0.11 before rising.
The final segment stays in the 0.55-0.65 range after the decline.
The marked 1990 point at 0.18 can be used as a visual anchor for the start of the steep rise.
unsupported_to_avoid: Absolute pay ratios such as 15-to-1 or 220-to-1, because the table has only relative_value.
Percentages, dollar amounts, counts, or any other absolute quantity not present in the table.
Causal claims about why CEO-worker pay gaps changed.
Extrapolating beyond the final relative_value or predicting future values.
Claiming the final value is the maximum; the maximum is 0.95, while the final value is 0.65.
Using x_px positions as semantic data or describing axis ticks, colors, or chart rendering.
notes: All cited numbers come from the relative_value column because the table has no absolute value. The intent supports overall widening, while the post-peak decline is marked optional because the narration emphasizes growth.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
